Quick summary in-line:
- Option Bronze (conservative): 8 x A100-80GB (min 8 GPUs reserved). Good for steady low-throughput customers; expected baseline latency SLOs, limited burst headroom.
- Option Silver (balanced): 16 x H100-80GB (min 16 GPUs reserved). Best for predictable throughput with room for growth; recommended for most of your ML workloads.
- Option Platinum (aggressive): 32 x H100 (min 24 GPUs reserved, 32 pooled). Intended for high-throughput inference; includes priority preemption lanes and expanded KV cache sizing.

Proposed ramp (example):
- Month 0–1: Provision min capacity (Bronze/Silver/Platinum baseline).
- Month 2: +50% capacity staged (automated warm-up; model pins and canary rollout).
- Month 3: Full committed capacity + burst policy enabled (automated fallback to hosted for non-sensitive traffic + overflow queueing for sensitive).

Adding runtime guidance and a quick sizing table (attached as Akora_cost_model_v2.xlsx). High-level:

- Assumptions: primary model is a 16k-context LLM with ~2.5 tokens/sec steady per H100 for batched requests (using our optimized kernels and kv-cache). Sequence distribution: 60% short (<512), 30% medium (512–4096), 10% long (>8k).

- Bronze (8 x A100-80GB): supports ~12 concurrent steady inference streams (p95 latency target ~220ms) — recommended only if Akora keeps model size <= 13B or uses aggressive quantization. Limited burst (hosted fallback recommended).

- Silver (16 x H100): supports ~40 concurrent steady streams with p95 latency ~120–160ms. Comfortable for most production traffic if they adopt batching and prefix caching. Suggested min commit: 16 GPUs.

- Platinum (32 x H100 with 24 min locked): supports ~90 concurrent streams, p95 ~80–110ms. Use this if they need predictable tail performance and low latency for high fan-out workloads. We recommend configuring KV cache to 1.5x model state for Platinum.

Fallback/overflow options:
- Soft-burst: auto-burst to hosted for non-PHI traffic (rate-limited, higher per-token cost).
- Queue + backpressure: for PHI traffic, place excess requests into a prioritized queue with retry window and SLA for completion.
- Emergency preempt pool: small reserved pool (2–4 GPUs) for critical endpoints to reduce cold-start risk.

I've attached the cost/capacity model and cluster_topology_sketch.png.

Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Agreed proposal (recommended path):
- Start with Silver baseline: 16 x H100 reserved (min commit: 16 GPUs).
- Ramp schedule:
  - Week 0 (contract start): Provision 16 GPUs; run warm-up tests and traffic canaries on non-prod endpoints.
  - Week 4: +25% capacity enabled (proactive scaling to 20 GPUs) tied to integration milestone sign-off.
  - Week 8: +50% capacity (24 GPUs) upon production validation (performance & latency thresholds met).
  - Week 12: Full planned capacity (32 GPUs) if utilization > 70% for two consecutive weeks; otherwise remain at 24 and revisit.

Commercial notes:
- Billing: monthly invoice with committed capacity charge + actual usage for burst beyond commitment. Burst into hosted is priced at +35% per-token over committed unit price.
- Early termination: standard 60-day notice with pro-rated credit for unused committed months after month 3.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool; emergency preempt pool (4 GPUs) included for critical routes.
